asks: How does Silo make the error for a denied tool call exist from where it sits?
answer: To find out, by a live check per program. The way to try first is the probe, the part of Silo that runs inside the computer. Silo keeps back the part of a reply that carries a tool call until it has read the call whole and the precaution has answered. When the precaution denies the call, Silo tells the probe and waits for the probe to say it is ready. Silo then passes the reply on unchanged. From then until the agent program's next request carries a result for that call, every new process and every file write that the agent program starts itself fails, apart from writes to its own files, such as its transcript of the conversation. Whatever the program does to run the call fails, and the program itself writes the error as the call's result. So the model sees its own call, unchanged, with an error, and Silo changes nothing in the traffic, then or when the conversation is resumed. When the probe does not say it is ready within a limit Silo sets, or the call is to a tool the probe cannot make fail, such as a local MCP server that is already running, Silo does not pass the reply on, and the agent program gets an error. The app then says that the model was not told why. Denying a tool call this way is a precaution's and never a rule's, since a rule is enforced outside the computer.
